It also says: "Nothing here has been tried on the tape, and nothing is claimed about it being good." (line 7) and the program says "Nothing here was scored." hypothesis: CL06's sentence about a crossed or locked quote can be applied to every rule's opening signal.
exact_claim: The page (inference 3): 'applying CL06's sentence to every rule. Only CL06's text says it.' This is the step condition 3 takes beyond CL06's text.
scope: Condition 3 (decider_v1/condition-3): every rule's opening signal. The page names no trade days and no dates; it says only that the decider was written with 'these trade days' already studied.
boundaries: Says nothing about whether other rules' texts allow a crossed quote; no other text was read as stating the exclusion. No outcome claimed.
inference_reason: Inferred from CL06's own text: the sentence 'Not while the best offer is at or below the best bid' is part of CL06's trigger and names CL06's rule only.
mechanism: A state in which the offer is at or below the bid is an abnormal quote; the decider treats the sentence CL06 writes for itself as a fact about the quote that holds for any rule's signal.
alternatives: Each rule's trigger is its own; a rule that states no such exclusion may be meant to act in that state.
CL06's clause may be there because its trigger reads two quotes' steps, which a crossed quote confuses, a reason that does not carry to rules reading one quote.
